studies.Reference: Are low ultraviolet B and high animal protein intake associated with risk of renal cancer?
studies.Title: Are low ultraviolet B and high animal protein intake associated with risk of renal cancer?
studies.Authors: Mohr SB, Gorham ED, Garland CF, Grant WB, Garland FC
studies.Population: Countries with cancer incidence data in the UN GLOBOCAN database providing dietary data
studies.comparison_type: Continuous association of intake of calories from animal sources with age-adjusted incidence rates in multiple regression

sample_size.excerpt: The independent association of UVB irradiance, cloud cover and intake of calories from animal sources with age-adjusted incidence rates was assessed using multiple regression in 139 countries that provided dietary data. Renal cancer incidence rates were highest in countries situated at the highest latitudes, in men (R(2) = 0.64, p < 0.01) and women (R(2) = 0.63, p < 0.01).

comparison.excerpt: The independent association of UVB irradiance, cloud cover and intake of calories from animal sources with age-adjusted incidence rates was assessed using multiple regression

design.excerpt: The association of latitude with age-adjusted incidence rates was determined for all 175 countries in a UN cancer database, GLOBOCAN.

continent.excerpt: all 175 countries in a UN cancer database, GLOBOCAN

exposure_measurement.excerpt: intake of calories from animal sources

gender.excerpt: According to multivariate analysis in men, UVB irradiance was inversely associated with renal cancer incidence rates

studies.context_id: 944046|Animal protein intake|Kidney and renal pelvis cancer
studies.Reference: A retrospective study of renal cancer with special reference to coffee and animal protein consumption.
studies.Title: A retrospective study of renal cancer with special reference to coffee and animal protein consumption.
studies.Authors: Armstrong B, Garrod A, Doll R
studies.Population: Patients diagnosed with renal cancer in the Oxford Regional Hospital Board area and selected London hospitals
studies.comparison_type: Renal cancer patients versus individually matched control patients

sample_size.excerpt: Interviews were obtained with 106 patients with adenocarcinoma of the renal parenchyma, 33 patients with carcinoma of the renal pelvis and 139 individually matched control patients.
sample_size.location: Results, Patients' characteristics, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 106 + 33 + 139 = 278

cases.excerpt: RESULTS Patients' characteristics A total of 139 pairs of patients with and without renal cancer were interviewed.

comparison.excerpt: Comparison of the cancer patients with the control patients showed no evidence of a positive association between either type of renal cancer and coffee or animal protein consumption.

design.excerpt: For each cancer patient, a control patient was selected at random, matched according to the following criteria: (1) same sex; (2) within the same 5-year age group; and (3)' having had a surgical operation in the same hospital

timing.excerpt: Notification was obtained of all patients diagnosed between 1 January 1972, and 31 December 1974, as suffering from renal cancer

continent.excerpt: Front the Department of the Regius Professor of Medicine and DHSS Cancer Epidemiology and Clinical Trials Unit, Radcliffe Infirmary, Oxford OX2 6HE

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Each cancer and each control patient was interviewed by a research assistant who was also a trained nurse.

gender.excerpt: Data on the age and sex of the renal cancer patients are shown in Table II.

smoking_status.excerpt: Renal cancer and control patients are compared with respect to tobacco use in Tables Vl and VI.
